title: Infrastructure as Code and What Terraform Does

header.html: 1a Explain what IaC is; 1b Describe the advantages of IaC patterns; 1c Explain how Terraform manages multi-cloud, hybrid cloud and service-agnostic workflows
the official Terraform Associate (004) exam content list

html:
1What infrastructure as code is

Infrastructure as code (IaC) means describing infrastructure in text files that a tool reads and applies, instead of clicking in a console or running one-off scripts.

Manual Infrastructure as code
Click in a console Write configuration files
Hard to repeat Repeatable in any environment
No history Version control records every change
Drift nobody sees The code is the documentation and the source of truth

Terraform is HashiCorp's IaC tool. You write configuration in HashiCorp Configuration Language (HCL) and Terraform creates, changes and destroys the infrastructure to match it.

Declarative: you describe the desired end state ("three servers"), and Terraform works out the steps. An imperative script lists the steps itself.

Exam tip

. Terraform is declarative. You say what you want; Terraform decides how to get there.

2Advantages of IaC patterns

Advantage Meaning
Automation and speed No manual steps; environments in minutes
Consistency and repeatability The same code gives the same result; fewer configuration differences
Version control History, review and rollback with Git
Collaboration Teams review changes before they are applied
Reduced errors and risk Fewer human mistakes; changes are previewed with a plan
Reusability Modules share patterns across teams
Cost control Create and destroy test environments on demand
Self-documentation The files describe what exists

3Terraform workflow in one line

Write the configuration → plan (preview the changes) → apply (make the changes). Details are in Module 4.

4Multi-cloud, hybrid cloud and service-agnostic

Idea How Terraform handles it
Multi-cloud Providers for AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and more; one workflow for all
Hybrid cloud Providers for on-premises systems too (virtualization platforms, Kubernetes)
Service-agnostic A provider can wrap any API: DNS, monitoring, version control, SaaS
One language HCL and the same commands everywhere

Terraform does not make the clouds the same: each provider's resource types differ. It gives one workflow, not one portable resource.

Exam tip

. Terraform manages infrastructure through providers, which talk to APIs. The workflow is the same; the resource types are provider-specific.

5Where Terraform fits

Tool kind Typical examples Focus
Provisioning (IaC) Terraform Create and manage infrastructure
Configuration management Ansible, Chef, Puppet Configure software on servers
Cloud-specific IaC CloudFormation, ARM templates One cloud
Exam tip

. If a question says describe the end state, it is declarative (Terraform). If it lists the steps, it is imperative. IaC stores the source of truth in files.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A team writes the desired number of servers in a file and lets the tool decide the steps. Which description fits?

  • AAn imperative script that lists the steps
  • BA manual process in the console
  • CA declarative approach, as Terraform uses
  • DA configuration management agent only
Show the answer

Answer: C. Terraform is declarative: you describe the desired end state and Terraform works out how to reach it.

S2A company wants every change to its infrastructure to be reviewed in Git before it happens. Which IaC advantage is this?

  • ALower prices from the cloud provider's sales team
  • BFaster internet connections
  • CAutomatic software licenses
  • DVersion control and collaboration
Show the answer

Answer: D. Storing the configuration in version control lets teams review, track and roll back changes.

S3How does Terraform support working with several clouds?

  • AIt makes every cloud use the same resource types
  • BIt uses providers and one common workflow
  • CIt only works with one provider at a time
  • DIt replaces the clouds' own APIs
Show the answer

Answer: B. Providers talk to each API, and the write, plan and apply workflow is the same everywhere.

S4Which statement about service-agnostic workflows is correct?

  • ATerraform can only manage virtual machines
  • BTerraform is limited to public clouds
  • CTerraform can manage any service that offers an API through a provider
  • DTerraform needs a separate language for each service
Show the answer

Answer: C. A provider can wrap any API, including DNS, monitoring or SaaS services.

S5Which benefit does IaC give when a test environment must be built and removed every week?

  • ARepeatable creation and destruction on demand
  • BHand-built servers with no history of changes
  • CPermanent environments that never change
  • DA console with more menus
Show the answer

Answer: A. Because the environment is code, it can be created and destroyed repeatedly with the same result.

S6What is the language used to write Terraform configuration called?

  • AYet Another Markup Language for infrastructure
  • BDomain Query Language
  • CResource Description Script
  • DHashiCorp Configuration Language
Show the answer

Answer: D. Terraform configuration is written in HashiCorp Configuration Language, HCL.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does IaC mean?

Show the answer

Describing infrastructure in code that a tool applies.

R2Is Terraform declarative or imperative?

Show the answer

Declarative.

R3Name two advantages of IaC.

Show the answer

For example repeatability and version control.

R4What lets Terraform manage many platforms?

Show the answer

Providers.

R5What is HCL?

Show the answer

The HashiCorp Configuration Language.

R6Does Terraform make all clouds use the same resource types?

Show the answer

No, resource types are provider-specific.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
IaC infrastructure described in files; code is the source of truth
Terraform declarative, HCL, providers, plan then apply
Advantages automation, consistency, version control, collaboration, fewer errors, reuse, cost
Scope multi-cloud, hybrid, any API; one workflow, provider-specific resources
